h1: Crawl Space Encapsulation in San Leandro, CA
description: Crawl space encapsulation in San Leandro, CA: vapor barriers and sealed crawl spaces that keep Bay Area moisture out. Get a free inspection.
intro: We seal crawl spaces against the damp air that comes up from the ground, with a vapor barrier, sealed vents and a dehumidifier where the space calls for one. Free inspection with a moisture reading.

sections.h2: Why East Bay crawl spaces stay wet
paragraphs: Crawl spaces pull in damp air through open vents, and the soil under the house keeps releasing moisture. In the East Bay the marine layer makes it worse: cool, humid air moves through the vents and condenses on the floor joists.
That damp feeds musty smells upstairs, warps wood over time, and makes the rest of the insulation work harder than it should.
Encapsulation means closing the crawl space off from outside air and ground moisture as one system, not just laying plastic.
bullets: Vapor barrier sealed up the foundation walls and around piers
Vent closure or a vented dehumidifier sized for the space
Optional floor insulation above the barrier

paragraphs: A loose barrier on the ground slows evaporation but does not stop humid outside air from moving through the vents. Encapsulation seals the space as a system, and that is what actually dries it out.
For most East Bay homes the difference shows within weeks: floors feel less cold, the musty smell fades, and the humidity reading inside the crawl space drops into a stable range.
Crawl space size, headroom and what is under there now set the price: a clean, tall space costs less to seal than a tight one with old debris, standing water or damaged piers.
We take moisture readings before and after and write the target humidity range into the estimate, so the result is measurable.
bullets: Fixed estimate after we see the space
Target humidity range stated up front

paragraphs: Once the space is sealed, we re-check it at the follow-up visit and adjust the dehumidifier settings if the readings call for it. A sealed crawl space also changes how we insulate the floor above, so we plan the two together instead of doubling back later.

steps.name: Inspection
steps.text: We measure the space, read the humidity and moisture levels, and check the vents, piers and rim joists.
steps.image_alt: Inspecting a crawl space with a moisture meter

steps.name: Prep
steps.text: Debris is removed and the ground is graded so the barrier can be laid tight to the walls.

steps.name: Seal
steps.text: The barrier is sealed up the walls and around piers, vents are closed, and the rim joist is sealed and insulated.
steps.image_alt: Sealing a vapor barrier up a foundation wall

steps.name: Verify
steps.text: We re-check humidity after the space settles and adjust the dehumidifier at the follow-up visit.
steps.image_alt: Reading humidity in a finished crawl space

faqs.q: How much does crawl space encapsulation cost?
faqs.a: It follows the size of the space and what is under there now. The inspection gives you a fixed written estimate based on your actual crawl space, not a square-foot guess.

faqs.q: Is encapsulation worth it for my house?
faqs.a: If the crawl space smells musty, floors feel damp-cold, or the humidity reading sits high, sealing it usually fixes all three at once and protects the joists from moisture damage.

faqs.q: Do I still need a dehumidifier after sealing?
faqs.a: Many sealed crawl spaces hold a stable range on their own, but low-lying or shady sites often need a small dehumidifier. We size it after the sealing is done, from the readings, not a catalog guess.

faqs.q: How long does the work take?
faqs.a: A standard crawl space takes one to two days depending on size and access. Tight or debris-filled spaces run longer, and we say so in the estimate.

faqs.q: Can you insulate the floor at the same time?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is usually the smart way: the barrier and the floor insulation work as one system, and doing both in one visit avoids a second mobilization.

faqs.q: Will the musty smell actually go away?
faqs.a: Sealing stops the damp air coming in, and the smell fades as the space dries out, usually within weeks. If odors linger, we re-check for leaks or standing water at the follow-up visit.
